title: The Crooked Crown Revisited
premise: Kestrel Ishikawa, a cartographer who maps the shifting smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains, discovers the old gods are answering prayers again when a dying pilgrim begs them to carry a message to King Aldric — a king Kestrel realizes has been dead for years, his body puppeted by the crown-spirit Veyra. Joining forces with the king's estranged daughter Princess Sable and a disgraced god of thresholds named Oren, Kestrel must reach the capital before the coronation rite that will make Veyra's possession permanent. Along the way Kestrel learns they were born in Thornfell's last god-touched village, marked as the vessel the old gods intended to reclaim. In the end, Kestrel chooses neither god nor crown but a third path: they redraw the map of the realm itself, giving the gods a country of their own drawn from unmapped space, freeing Aldric's spirit to die and Sable to inherit a kingdom learning to share its edges with the divine.
about_author: S. M. Hartwell is the pen name of a former trail surveyor who spent six seasons mapping passes no government would officially acknowledge. They write fantasy about people who know that borders, like maps, are only ever provisional.

chapters.title: The Road That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. While surveying a smuggler route through Thornfell, Kestrel finds a pass that appears on none of their maps — and watches it close behind them like a healing wound. The emotional beat is unease: a professional's confidence cracking as the landscape itself begins lying.

chapters.title: A Pilgrim's Last Request
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A starving pilgrim stumbles into their camp, praying aloud to gods Kestrel assumed were myths — and receives an answer. Dying, she entrusts Kestrel with a sealed message for King Aldric. Beat: reluctant responsibility; Kestrel takes the letter mostly to be rid of her ghost.

chapters.title: The Letter That Should Not Be Delivered
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, with an interlude from the letter itself written in Aldric's hand years ago. Reading it in secret, Kestrel learns the king wrote it before his supposed death. Beat: vertigo — the world's official history and its living truth have diverged.

chapters.title: Princess Sable, Under House Arrest
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the capital, Sable notices her father never blinks during audiences and smells of cold stone instead of skin. She has been confined 'for her safety.' Beat: dread sharpening into resolve as she confirms something wears her father.

chapters.title: Oren at the Doorway
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Pursued by crown soldiers on the mountain road, Kestrel is saved by a ragged man who steps them through a doorway onto the far side of the range. He claims to be Oren, god of thresholds, exiled and fading. Beat: wary alliance born of necessity.

chapters.title: What the Gods Want
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Around a fire, Oren explains the old gods were bound out of the world generations ago; recently their bindings frayed, and something older slipped through first — Veyra, the thing in the crown. Beat: revelation reframing everything Kestrel mapped as scars of the binding.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Any Map
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Oren leads Kestrel to ruins Kestrel recognizes from childhood dreams: Thornfell's last god-touched village, burned in the binding wars. Among the ashes Kestrel finds a birth-record bearing their own name. Beat: identity upended — Kestrel was born here, marked.

chapters.title: Vessel
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, intimate and interior. Kestrel confronts what the record means: the old gods made them as a vessel, a body prepared to hold divinity. Beat: anger and grief — every choice in their life suddenly suspect, even their love of maps.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Amber Court
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel and Sable POVs. Using smuggler routes, Kestrel and Oren enter the capital; Sable, escaping her confinement, nearly catches them stealing court keys. Beat: friction turning to trust as each recognizes the other's competence and loneliness.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable engineers a private meeting between Kestrel and the king. Up close, Aldric's eyes hold a flicker of the real man, who mouths one word: daughter. Beat: heartbreak — some of Aldric survives inside his own stolen body.

chapters.title: Veyra Speaks
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV, the book's first glimpse inside the antagonist. Veyra is not mindless evil but a god of order starved for worship, convinced unification under one will is mercy. Beat: chilling sympathy — the villain believes herself the cure.

chapters.title: The Coronation Rite
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Court documents reveal the rite scheduled at midwinter will fuse Veyra permanently to the throne and, through it, the realm's ley-lines. Beat: ticking clock established — weeks, not months.

chapters.title: Found Family, Improvised
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Hiding in a smuggler safehouse, the fugitives — cartographer, princess, faded god, plus young pickpocket Wren who attaches herself to them — share a quiet chapter of meals, mending, and stories. Beat: warmth; the found family crystallizes before the storm.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. To buy supplies, Wren sells information about the group to a court spymaster, then immediately regrets it. Beat: guilt and loyalty tested; she confesses, and the family absorbs rather than expels her.

chapters.title: The Binding Beneath the City
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Guided by ley-line sense, the group finds the original binding-stone beneath the palace — and discovers Kestrel's blood is the key that both locked and can unlock it. Beat: terrible clarity about why Kestrel was made.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Stone
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Crown guards, tipped by the spymaster, ambush them at the stone. Oren burns most of his remaining divinity to get the others out and is captured. Beat: sacrifice and despair; the plan lies in pieces.

chapters.title: What Kestrel Chooses
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Offered safety if they flee, Kestrel refuses to be either weapon or victim, deciding to fight the terms of their own creation. Beat: agency reclaimed — identity defined by choice, not origin.

chapters.title: Storming the Coronation
chapters.summary: Alternating Kestrel, Sable, and Wren POVs. Midwinter day: Sable stalls the rite from within, Wren opens hidden ways through the palace, Kestrel walks the nave toward the crown. Beat: kinetic climax building, every thread converging.

chapters.title: The Crooked Crown
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Face to face with Veyra, Kestrel refuses the role of vessel — and instead offers her a bargain: not a realm to consume, but a country to draw. Beat: the climax pivots on imagination over force.

chapters.title: A Country Drawn from Nothing
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Using their cartographer's gift, Kestrel sketches new borders into unmapped space, and the old gods pour into the blank land rather than into Kestrel or the throne. Veyra, given true dominion, releases Aldric. Beat: transcendent release.

chapters.title: Goodbye, Father
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Freed, Aldric has hours, not years. He and Sable say what the crown never let them say; he dies at dawn holding her hand. Beat: grief braided with peace and the weight of inheritance.

chapters.title: Edges Shared
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, closing. Months later: Queen Sable rules a realm whose maps now show two countries, Kestrel redrawing boundaries with the gods' consent, Wren apprenticed, Oren tending doorways again. Beat: resolution — love, family, and identity all chosen rather than assigned.
